GEORGIA POWER COMPANY
	
	Jeremiah Haswell
	Director, Regulatory Affairs	
	Georgia Power Company
	Regulatory Affairs Bin 10230
	241 Ralph McGill Blvd., N.E.
	Atlanta, Georgia 30308-3374

	COMES NOW the Staff of the Georgia Public Service Commission (“Commission”) and, pursuant to the authority vested in it by the Commission pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-2-57, herein propounds the following interrogatories and requests for production of documents (collectively, “data requests”), to be answered under oath by designated representatives or agents of Georgia Power Company.  Staff requests that a complete set of the responses and supporting documents be filed with the Commission’s Executive Secretary in the manner set forth in Utility Rule 515-2-.04(4).  Staff requests that an original and five (5) copies be filed with the Executive Secretary of the Commission.  Accompanied therewith shall be an electronic version of the filing, which shall be made on a 3 ½ inch diskette or a CD ROM containing an electronic version of its filing in Microsoft Word® for text documents or Excel® for spreadsheets.  As contemplated by law, responses to these Data Requests are expected from Georgia Power Company on or before October 22, 2026. 


DEFINITIONS

As may be used in this document:  
1.	“The Company,” “Georgia Power” or “The Utility” means Georgia Power Company and its present and former officers, employees, agents, representatives, directors, and all other persons acting or purporting to act on behalf of said Company.
The term “you” and “your” refer to “the Company.”
The term “person” means any natural person, corporation, corporate division, partnership, other unincorporated association, trust, government agency, or entity.
The term “document” or “documentation” shall have the broadest possible meaning under applicable law.  “Document” or “documentation” means every writing or record of every type and description that is in the possession, custody or control of the Company including, but not limited to, correspondence, memoranda, e-mails, drafts, workpapers, summaries, stenographic or handwritten notes, studies, notices, publications, books, pamphlets, reports, surveys, minutes or statistical compilations, computer and other electronic records or tapes or printouts, including, but not limited to, electronic mail files; and copies of such writing or records containing any commentary or notation whatsoever that does not appear in the original.  The term “document” or “documentation” further includes, by way of illustration and not limitation, schedules, progress schedules, time logs, drawings, computer disks, chart projections, time tables, summaries of other documents, minutes, surveys, work sheets, drawings, comparisons, evaluations, laboratory and testing reports, telephone call records, personal diaries, calendars, personal notebooks, personal reading files, transcripts, witness statements and indices.
The term “referring or relating to” means consisting of, containing, mentioning, suggesting, reflecting, concerning, regarding, summarizing, analyzing, discussing, involving, dealing with, emanating from, directed at, pertaining to in any way, or in any way logically or factually connected or associated with the matter discussed.
“And” and “or” as used herein shall be construed both conjunctively and disjunctively and each shall include the other whenever such construction will serve to bring within the scope of these discovery requests any information that would not otherwise be brought within their scope.
The singular as used herein shall include the plural and the masculine gender shall include the feminine and the neuter.
“Identify” or “identifying” or “identification” when used in reference to a person other than a natural person means to state:  the full name of the person and any names under which it conducts business; the present or last known address of the person; and, the present or last known telephone number of the person.
“Identify” or “identifying” or “identification” when used in reference to a document means to provide with respect to each document requested to be identified by these discovery requests a description of the document that is sufficient for purposes of a request to produce or a subpoena duces tecum, including the following:						
the type of document (e.g., letter, memorandum, etc.);
the date of the document; the title or label of the document;
the Bates number or other identifier used to number the document for use in  litigation; the identity of the originator;
the identity of each person to whom it was sent;
the identity of each person to whom a copy or copies were sent;
a summary of the contents of the document;
the name and last known address of each person who presently has possession, custody or control of the document;
if any such document was, but is no longer, in your possession,  custody or control or is no longer in existence, state whether it: (1) is missing or lost; (2) has been destroyed; or (3) has been transferred voluntarily or involuntarily, and if so, state the circumstances surrounding the authorization for each such disposition and the date of such disposition.					
“Identify”, “identifying” or identity” when used in reference to a communication should be read to include information regarding the date of the communication, whether the communication was written or oral, the identity of all parties and witnesses to the communication, the substance of what was said and/or transpired and, if written, the identity of the document(s) containing or referring to the communication.


INSTRUCTIONS
If you contend that any response to any data request may be withheld under the attorney-client privilege, the attorney work product doctrine or any other privilege or basis, please state the following with respect to each such response in order to explain the basis for the claim of privilege and to permit adjudication of the propriety of that claim:	
the privilege asserted and its basis.
the nature of the information withheld;
the subject matter of the document, except to the extent that you claim it is privileged.
The answers provided should first restate the question asked and also provide the name of the Company employee(s) or agents responsible for compiling and providing the information contained in each answer. 
These data requests are to be answered with reference to all information in your possession, custody or control or reasonably available to you.  These discovery requests are intended to include requests for information, which is physically within your possession, custody or control as well as in the possession, custody or control of your agents, attorneys, or other third parties from which such documents may be obtained.
If any data request cannot be responded to or answered in full, answer to the extent possible and specify the reasons for your inability to answer fully.
These data requests are continuing in nature and require supplemental responses should information unknown to you at the time you serve your responses to these interrogatories subsequently become known.
If you contend that any response to any data request may be withheld under the attorney-client privilege, the attorney work product doctrine or any other privilege or basis, please state the following with respect to each such response in order to explain the basis for the claim of privilege and to permit adjudication of the propriety of that claim:  
the privilege asserted and its basis.
a log should be provided identifying starting and ending bates numbers.
the nature of the information withheld;
the subject matter of the document, except to the extent that you claim it is privileged.
a description of the document to which the privilege applies. 


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

Is the $xxx million payment from the customer split between Georgia Power and the other Hatch co-owners? If yes, identify the split between Georgia Power and Hatch co-owners. If no, confirm Georgia Power would retain the entire $xxx million payment.

Ratemaking treatment of $xxx million payment: Would the Company object to placing the $ xxx million in a regulatory liability and applying the regulatory liability against the Hatch 1&2 CWIP balance for the duration of the construction period?

Are the revenues from “Zero emission credits” from the customer split between Georgia Power and the other Hatch co-owners? If yes, identify the split between Georgia Power and Hatch co-owners. If no, confirm Georgia Power would retain all the revenues from “Zero emission credit” payments from the customer.

Ratemaking treatment of “Zero emission credits” revenues: Would the Company object to “Zero emission credits” revenues being directly applied against Hatch 1&2 O&M expense?

In B26_AV_Tool_HatchEPU - GPC Ownership TRADE SECRET.xlsx, explain the difference between Incremental Capital and Baseline Capital. 

Is there a cost cap associated with the nuclear uprates at Hatch 1 and 2? 

In the event the Hatch 1 and 2 uprates exceed the estimated budget, will the Company agree to not seek recovery of the additional costs from all ratepayers? 

In response to Informal STF-NU1-1-7 that Company stated, “The Company anticipates that customer agreements will be for a 25-year term, consistent with the program's capital recovery structure and the subscriber’s long-term clean energy commitments. There is no minimum term threshold required under the NU-1 Tariff.” In the event customers do not agree to a 25-year term, is there a guarantee from the Company that all ZECs will be purchased over the remaining life of the units? 

Has the Company performed any analysis of similar Extended Power Uprate (EPU) projects completed by other utilities (such as Monticello or Grand Gulf), whether through NRC filings, published documentation, or industry communications? If so, please provide a summary of the key findings.
If the Company has performed such analyses, has the Company accounted for initial man-hours and component prices quoted compared to final cost? 

How has the Company accounted for financial risk, including potential cost overruns, when performing its budget analysis? 

Can the Company confirm whether there are any contingency funds to address cost exceeding the budget?

Refer to the Company’s draft Nuclear Uprates “NU-1” Electric Service Tariff. The new tariff availability states: “Available throughout Georgia Power Company’s service area.” Does the service territory include all large load customers being served by Georgia Power Company, including those being served as a result of the customer choice program?  

“An eligible customer wishing to subscribe to the NU-1 tariff must submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) to sponsor the nuclear uprate program and pay a one-time sponsorship fee.” How long will the NOI period be open? How much is the sponsorship fee? Please describe how the amount was determined and provide workpapers supporting any calculations used to determine the amount.  

“The NU-1 tariff enables customers to sponsor nuclear uprates at existing, certified nuclear facilities (Nuclear Uprate Portfolio) within the Georgia Power fleet.” What are the uprate costs for each unit? What are the estimated administrative expenses associated with the tariff for each of the next ten years? 

“Each participating customer will pay a Program Enrollment Contribution (PEC) and an NU-1 tariff Monthly Subscription Payment that will be separate and in addition to the cost of electric service under the customer’s then-existing retail electric service tariff. In exchange for the Monthly Subscription Payment, each participating customer will receive zero emission credits (ZECs) in an amount based on the customer’s subscription level and the corresponding pro-rata share of the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).” How will the PEC and Monthly Subscription Payment amounts be calculated? Please provide the Company’s estimates for the PEC and monthly subscription payment.

“The PEC amount and price of ZECs will be defined in the customer agreement. The ZECs associated with the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio will be allocated according to each customer’s subscription level and the corresponding pro-rata share of the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio.” Provide a pro forma customer agreement with sample pricing for the PEC and ZECs. 

“The ZECs associated with the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio will be allocated according to each customer’s subscription level and the corresponding pro-rata share of the output of the Nuclear Uprate Portfolio … The NU-1 Monthly Subscription Payment will be calculated by multiplying the price of ZECs by the quantity of energy deemed produced by the nuclear uprate capacity share during the billing period. The PEC payment amount will be defined in the customer agreement.” Provide a sample bill or invoice with calculations in Microsoft Excel and all formulas intact. 

“To subscribe to the NU-1 tariff, a customer must execute a customer agreement with Georgia Power. The customer’s subscription term under the NU-1 tariff will coincide with the term of the Nuclear Uprate Customer Agreement as selected by the customer during the NOI process. Such term may be up to 25 years.” Is there a minimum subscription term under the tariff (e.g. 10 years, 15 years)? 

“If Georgia Power terminates a customer agreement due to an event of default by customer, the customer will be responsible for damages and payments in accordance with the customer’s agreement.” How is default defined in the customer agreement? How will damages be calculated?  

Please explain how the NU-1 tariff will benefit non-subscribing customers of Georgia Power.  

What happens to the incremental revenue from the NU-1 tariff? Identify and explain the accounting treatment for all revenue and expenses associated with the tariff. Does this accounting treatment differ from what is required by accounting standards? Regarding the proposed accounting treatment, what specifically does Georgia Power have to receive approval from the Commission?




Please identify and explain the required financial contribution prior to achievement of uprates at Hatch. Provide an example with all accounting entries associated with the contribution. 

Refer to the PowerPoint presentation dated March 19, 2026 “Nuclear Uprates Subscription and NU-1 Tariff”. Please define the accounting deferrals referenced on page 3.  

Refer to the PowerPoint presentation dated March 19, 2026 “Nuclear Uprates Subscription and NU-1 Tariff”. Provide workpapers with formulas intact and all assumptions for Table 1 Projected Nuclear Uprate Tariff Revenue and Table 2 EPU Cost-Benefit Results for Hatch 1-2. 

Refer to the PowerPoint presentation dated March 19, 2026 “Nuclear Uprates Subscription and NU-1 Tariff”. Provide a copy of the heat balance analyses, scheduled for completion in March 2026, to validate these assumptions related to the Hatch 1-2 EPU and projected efficiency gains. 

Are ZECs subsequently tradeable or does retiring ZECs on behalf of the customer mean they are not subsequently tradeable? 

Are there any guarantees associated with estimated revenue associated with the NU-1 tariff, either in the contracts or elsewhere? Please explain.  

If NU-1 subscribers terminate and other large load customers do not subsequently subscribe to the tariff (e.g. they have a different view of additionality), what would be the potential impacts on Georgia Power’s other customers (those to whom NU-1 is not available)?  

How are the Vogtle Unit 1 and 2 uprates qualified as additional? 

Provide the Company’s cost-benefit analysis workpapers associated with the NU-1 tariff. 



Based on the costs discussed during the 3/19 meeting with Staff, how many customers do the Company anticipate will enroll in this tariff?  

In the event that Commission Staff do not recommend certification of the Hatch Unit upgrades before customers sign customer agreements fully committing to pay for the uprates, explain why customer agreements cannot include a contingency, or “regulatory out,” providing that the agreement would be terminated in the event that the Commission does not approve the upgrades. 

Will Georgia Power provide any compensation to subscribers for decreased nuclear output due to planned or unplanned outages, failure to uprate at expected levels, or any other situations where it does not produce nuclear power?  How will other customers be protected from these penalties and the additional costs, including fuel costs, of powering the grid without these resources? 

Provide a list of all large load customers and large load customer representatives with whom Georgia Power has discussed the nuclear uprate tariff and describe the nature of the discussions. 

Provide a copy of all electronic correspondence with large load customers, including representatives, regarding the nuclear uprate tariff. 

Provide a list of all large load customers, including representatives, with whom Georgia Power has discussed the Hatch 1-2 EPU and describe the nature of the discussions. 

Provide a copy of all electronic correspondence with large load customers, including representatives, regarding the Hatch 1-2 EPU.
